facts.statement: The type species Klamelisaurus gobiensis was named by Zhao Xijin in 1993 based on a partial skeleton found in 1982 near the abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao.
facts.quote: The type species is Klamelisaurus gobiensis, which was named by Zhao Xijin in 1993, based on a partial skeleton discovered in 1982 near the abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao.

facts.statement: The skeleton was discovered 35 km north of the abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao in the eastern Junggar Basin in 1982.
facts.quote: In 1982, these excavations uncovered the skeleton of a sauropod dinosaur 35 km north of the now-abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao, located in the eastern Junggar Basin.

facts.statement: Preparation and restoration of the specimen began in 1985 after it was transported to Beijing.
facts.quote: After it was transported to Beijing, with preparation and restoration work beginning in 1985, it deteriorated further due to fluctuations in temperature and humidity.

facts.statement: The specimen was redescribed by Andrew Moore and colleagues in 2020 after receiving limited attention following its initial description.
facts.quote: Following Zhao's description, IVPP V9492 received limited attention in the literature until it was redescribed by Andrew Moore and colleagues in 2020.

facts.statement: Klamelisaurus was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic in the Shishugou Formation of China.
facts.quote: Klamelisaurus (meaning "Kelameili Mountains lizard") is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Shishugou Formation of China.

facts.statement: Klamelisaurus was approximately 13 meters long, with its neck accounting for half of its total length.
facts.quote: A relatively large sauropod measuring approximately 13 m long, with half of the length being its neck, Klamelisaurus can be distinguished from its relatives by characteristics of the vertebrae and humerus.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 13 meters and weight at 6 tons in 2016, based on the hypothesis that the specimen represented an adult form.
facts.quote: In 2016, American paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 13 m in length and 6 t in weight, albeit based on the hypothesis that Klamelisaurus represented the adult form of Bellusaurus.

facts.statement: Zhao originally classified Klamelisaurus as the sole member of the new subfamily Klamelisaurinae within the order Bothrosauropodoidea.
facts.quote: Zhao described Klamelisaurus as the only member of a new subfamily, Klamelisaurinae, among the now-defunct primitive sauropod order Bothrosauropodoidea.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest Klamelisaurus belongs to the family Mamenchisauridae, a group of primarily Chinese sauropods.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses have suggested that Klamelisaurus belonged to the Mamenchisauridae, a group of Middle to Late Jurassic and primarily Chinese sauropods, although its close relatives also include a mamenchisaurid from Thailand.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Bellusaurus is a juvenile Klamelisaurus has been rejected due to anatomical differences and geological age differences.
facts.quote: While paleontologist Gregory S. Paul suggested that Bellusaurus, known only from juvenile specimens, was a juvenile Klamelisaurus, this proposal has been rejected based on anatomical evidence, and the fact that Bellusaurus was geologically younger.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Klamelisaurus preserves nine neck vertebrae, with an estimated total of sixteen and a total length of 6.5 meters.
facts.quote: Zhao stated that the type specimen of Klamelisaurus preserved nine cervicals (neck vertebrae), out of an estimated total of sixteen with a total length of 6.5 m.

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues identified irregular, plate-like extensions on the spinoprezygapophyseal laminae of Klamelisaurus neck vertebrae as a unique feature.
facts.quote: Moore and colleagues noted two unique features (autapomorphies) in the cervicals. First, the spinoprezygapophyseal laminae (SPRLs), ridges of bone extending forward from the neural spines, bore irregular, plate-like extensions.

facts.statement: Deep openings were found on the sides of the neck vertebrae below the spinoprezygapophyseal laminae and in front of the spinodiapophyseal fossae in Klamelisaurus.
facts.quote: Second, below the SPRLs and in front of depressions called the spinodiapophyseal fossae (SDFs), the sides of the centra bore a set of deep foramina (openings).

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues identified twelve dorsal and six sacral vertebrae in the type specimen of Klamelisaurus.
facts.quote: Moore and colleagues identified twelve dorsals and six sacrals in the type specimen of Klamelisaurus.

facts.statement: Klamelisaurus dorsal vertebrae were opisthocoelous with shallow openings and simple ridges, had low neural spines that were two-pronged at the front and expanded at the back, and had fused sacral centra and spines.
facts.quote: Zhao's diagnosis noted that the dorsals were opisthocoelous; the dorsals had shallow pleurocoels (neurovascular openings) and simple lamination (ridging); the dorsal neural spines were low, with the first few being bifid and the last few having expanded tips; the sacral centra were fused such that their boundaries were not visible; and the first four sacral neural spines were fused.

facts.statement: Some dorsal vertebrae of Klamelisaurus possessed sets of three posterior centroparapophyseal laminae, a feature identified as unique by Moore and colleagues.
facts.quote: Moore and colleagues identified two unique features in the dorsals. First, the sides of some of the dorsals bore sets of three posterior centroparapophyseal laminae (PCPLs).

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues found parts of nineteen tail vertebrae in the Klamelisaurus specimen, including spines and centra from various sections of the tail.
facts.quote: Parts of nineteen caudals (tail vertebrae) were found by Moore and colleagues: parts of the first four caudals (labelled as caudals 1–4), five more neural spines from the front of the tail (labelled as caudals 6 and 8–11), and eleven centra from the middle of the tail (labelled as caudals 18–27 and 33).

facts.statement: Zhao estimated that Klamelisaurus originally had sixty tail vertebrae with a total length of 6.55 meters based on his count of preserved elements.
facts.quote: Zhao originally counted two complete caudals, ten neural spines from the front, and ten middle centra, based on which he estimated that sixty were originally present with a total length of 6.55 m.

facts.statement: The front tail vertebrae of Klamelisaurus were procoelous while the rest were amphicoelous, and the tail neural spines were thicker at the tip and slanted sharply backward.
facts.quote: Zhao's list of characteristics indicated that the first few caudals were procoelous (with centra concave in front and convex behind), with the rest being amphicoelous (with centra concave on both ends); and the caudal neural spines were claviform (thicker at the tip) and slanted extremely to the rear.

facts.statement: Klamelisaurus differs from Tienshanosaurus by having procoelous front tail vertebrae and neural spine tips slanted so far back they reach behind the postzygapophyses.
facts.quote: Characteristics of the caudals that differentiate Klamelisaurus from Tienshanosaurus include the procoelous front caudals, and the front edge of the tip of the neural spines being slanted to the point of reaching behind the rear edge of the processes known as postzygapophyses.

facts.statement: Zhao indicated that the forelimb of Klamelisaurus was three-quarters the length of the hindlimb, with the ulna and tibia being two-thirds the length of the humerus and femur respectively.
facts.quote: In terms of limb proportions, Zhao indicated that the forelimb of Klamelisaurus was three-quarters the length of the hindlimb, and the ulna and tibia were respectively two-thirds the lengths of the humerus and femur.

facts.statement: The top of the Klamelisaurus humerus was thick and slightly curved, lacking the overhanging sub-circular process found in Bellusaurus and many neosauropods.
facts.quote: Zhao observed that the top of the humerus was thick, and slightly curved. Unlike Bellusaurus and many neosauropods, the head of the humerus did not have an overhanging sub-circular process.

facts.statement: Zhao suggested the expansion of the upper ulna in Klamelisaurus was unique, but Moore and colleagues found it comparable to many other sauropods.
facts.quote: Zhao n that the ulna was longer than the relatively straight radius, and he suggested that the degree of expansion of the upper ulna was unique; Moore and colleagues instead found that it was comparable to many other sauropods.

facts.statement: Unlike Bellusaurus, the anteromedial process at the top of the Klamelisaurus ulna had a convex surface that sloped below the olecranon process.
facts.quote: Also unlike Bellusaurus, the anteromedial process at the top of the ulna had a convex (not flat) surface that sloped below the olecranon process.

facts.statement: Zhao diagnosed Klamelisaurus as having a robust ilium, slender ischium, reconstructed pubis, thick flat femur with a fourth trochanter near the top, and a tibia shorter than the fibula.
facts.quote: Zhao's diagnosis for the hips and legs of Klamelisaurus included a robust ilium with an indistinct "laminar ridge" and a forward-projecting pubic peduncle (attachment to the pubis); a slender ischium; a robust, thin, flat, and weakly curved pubis (however, this bone appears to be reconstructed); a thick and flat femur with an indistinct head and a fourth trochanter (the attachment for the caudofemoralis muscle) located near the top of the bone; and a tibia shorter than the fibula (however, these bones are either incomplete or heavily reconstructed).

facts.statement: In 1993, Zhao classified Klamelisaurus as the sole genus in the new subfamily Klamelisaurinae.
facts.quote: In his 1993 description, Zhao placed Klamelisaurus as the only genus in a new subfamily, Klamelisaurinae

facts.statement: Zhao described Klamelisaurus as an early to middle stage sauropod possessing transitional characters.
facts.quote: He considered it to be "early to middle stage sauropod" with "transitional characters"

facts.statement: Zhao placed Klamelisaurus within the Brachiosauridae under his definition of the group.
facts.quote: Within the "early stage" Bothrosauropodoidea, Zhao considered Klamelisaurus to be part of the Brachiosauridae

facts.statement: Later scientific literature has not adopted Zhao's specific taxonomic classification for Klamelisaurus.
facts.quote: Subsequent literature has not used Zhao's taxonomy for Klamelisaurus

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues termed the group containing Klamelisaurus and related sauropods the "core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa".
facts.quote: They termed these the "core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa"

facts.statement: Most analyses found the core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa, including Klamelisaurus, to be closely related to Euhelopus, Daxiatitan, and Dongbeititan.
facts.quote: Nearly all of their analyses found the "core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa" to be closely related to Euhelopus, Daxiatitan, and Dongbeititan, traditionally considered part of the more derived Macronaria

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues recovered the wider group containing Klamelisaurus, termed Euhelopodidae, outside of the Neosauropoda.
facts.quote: They recovered this wider group — which they termed the Euhelopodidae — outside of the Neosauropoda

facts.statement: Researchers highlighted the need for further redescriptions and revisions of sauropods like Mamenchisaurus and Omeisaurus to resolve classification debates.
facts.quote: Thus, they highlighted a need for further redescriptions and revisions of these sauropods (particularly Mamenchisaurus and Omeisaurus) as well as the development of more distinguishing characteristics

facts.statement: Paul suggested in 2010 and 2016 that Klamelisaurus might be the adult form of Bellusaurus.
facts.quote: In The Princeton Field Guide to Dinosaurs, a popular book with two editions published in 2010 and 2016, Paul has suggested that Klamelisaurus may have been be the adult form of Bellusaurus

facts.statement: In 2018, Moore and colleagues refuted the hypothesis that Klamelisaurus is the adult form of Bellusaurus.
facts.quote: In 2018, Moore and colleagues redescribed Bellusaurus and provided several arguments to refute this notion

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues noted that Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus were not contemporaries, as the Klamelisaurus holotype comes from older rock layers.
facts.quote: First, they noted that the two were not actually contemporaries; the holotype of Klamelisaurus originates from slightly older strata (rock layers)

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues identified differences in vertebral pneumatic features between Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus that cannot be explained by age differences.
facts.quote: Most of the characteristics on their list pertain to differences in pneumatic features in the vertebrae of Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus that are not readily explainable by differences in age

facts.statement: Bellusaurus possessed specific pneumatic features in dorsal neural spines and arches that Klamelisaurus lacked, contradicting expected patterns for euhelopodids and mamenchisaurids.
facts.quote: However, they noted that Bellusaurus possessed several pneumatic features in the dorsal neural spines and neural arches that Klamelisaurus lacked, which runs contrary to the expected pattern for euhelopodids and mamenchisaurids

facts.statement: Moore and colleagues noted that bifurcated neural spines and wing-shaped processes on rear dorsals might vary with age, complicating the distinction between Klamelisaurus and Bellusaurus.
facts.quote: However, they also noted two characteristics on their list which may have varied with age: the bifurcated neural spines, and the presence of wing-shaped processes that projected further outwards than the postzygapophyses on the rear dorsals

facts.statement: The species Klamelisaurus gobiensis was described by Zhao Xijin in 1993.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, K. gobiensis, fue descrita por Zhao Xijin en 1993.

facts.quote: El holotipo , IVPP V9492, se encontró en una capa de la formación Shishugou que data del Oxfordiano, de unos 160 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.

facts.statement: The postcranial skeleton is fairly complete, missing only the front of the neck, the left shoulder girdle, the left forelimb, and the feet.

facts.quote: Zhao en 1993 estableció una única autapomorfia explícita, el extremo superior del cúbito se expande.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 15 meters and weight at 5 tons, assuming it represented the adult form of Bellusaurus.

facts.statement: In 1993, Zhao erected a new subfamily, Klamelisaurinae, of which Klamelisaurus was the only member.
facts.quote: En 1993 Zhao erigió una nueva subfamilia, Klamelisaurinae, de la cual Klamelisaurus era el único miembro.

facts.statement: Zhao assigned Klamelisaurinae to the obscure sauropod clade Bothrosauropodea.
facts.quote: Asignó Klamelisaurinae al oscuro clado de saurópodos Bothrosauropodea.

facts.statement: Upchurch et al. considered its classification uncertain in 2004, possibly being a non-neosauropod eusauropod.

facts.statement: The parent group of Klamelisaurus is Mamenchisauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mamenchisauridae

facts.statement: It lived during the middle Jurassic, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago in the Oxfordian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 165 a 161 millones de años en el Oxfordiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The time range is the Callovian, from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
